summary: Baseline before new changes using current branch defaults.
Set Q expression scheduling weight to 10 and use four host proof workers.
Prioritize compressor-capable basic proofs before stored-only proofs in proof scheduling.
Stage large Q expression bytecode in shared-memory tiles during GPU interpretation.
Inline Poseidon partial-round state summation to reduce hash dependency overhead.
Register witness host buffers once and use serialized direct H2D copies from registered source memory.
Generate a register-resident kernel for expression 4152 to remove shared-temp traffic on that Q evaluation.
Use two basic GPU streams to free memory for seven recursive proof streams.
Preserve witness scheduling order and use 24 recursive witness workers to reduce small-block proof latency while keeping the large block below target.
Generate a standalone kernel for Q expression 4297, removing its repeated generic interpreter fallback on large domains.
Reuse custom fixed commits when a stream keeps the same AIR context, avoiding redundant fixed-data H2D copies.
Skip satisfied cached native recursive solve-plan steps and materialize recursive committed traces in one pass.
Use byte-backed native recursive known-state tracking instead of Rust bit-packed Vec<bool> to reduce high-frequency solver access overhead.
Use uninitialized prover-side proof output buffers where the C/GPU path overwrites the proof contents, avoiding redundant zero-fill before proof generation.
Skip all-zero chunks while fingerprinting native recursive known-state bytes, reducing wasted scans on sparse large witnesses.
Use default cudaHostRegister flags for witness host buffers, avoiding portable registration on the single-GPU same-NUMA path while keeping direct H2D copies enabled.
Use direct u64 field extraction, read locks, and already-loaded recursive verkeys when assembling recursive public inputs, removing BigUint conversion and repeated verkey JSON reads.
